notes.meaning: Love must always be the main goal in a Christian's life. At the same time, believers should eagerly want the gifts the Holy Spirit gives to help others. Among these gifts, prophecy is especially valuable because it shares God's truth in plain words.

differ.view: Many evangelicals believe miraculous gifts have ended, so they understand prophecy here as inspired preaching from the Bible.
Charismatics believe prophecy continues today as a supernatural gift and should not be reduced to ordinary preaching.

notes.meaning: A person who speaks in an unknown tongue is speaking directly to God rather than to other people. The listeners cannot understand the speech because the speaker is declaring divine mysteries by the Spirit. Without an interpreter, the words do not communicate truth to the gathering.

A person who prophesies speaks in normal words that everyone in the room can understand. Their speech helps the listeners by building up their faith, urging them forward in duty, and comforting them in sadness. This makes the gift immediately helpful to the entire gathering.

A person speaking in an unknown tongue strengthens only their own personal faith. In contrast, someone who prophesies strengthens the faith of the whole church assembly. Christians should aim to help others rather than keep blessings to themselves.

Paul would be pleased if every believer had the gift of tongues, but he desires even more that they prophesy. Prophecy holds a higher place in public worship because it does more good for the listeners. Tongues can only equal prophecy when someone translates them so the church can be built up.

If Paul came visiting and spoke only in languages no one knew, his visit would be of no value to the church. To help the believers, he must bring clear knowledge, biblical teaching, or a message from God in words they understand. Good communication always focuses on what helps the hearer.

Musical instruments like flutes or harps do not produce real music if they play only one unchanging tone. People cannot recognize a song unless the notes are separated and distinct. In the same way, human speech must have clear sounds to make any sense.

In an army, a trumpet is blown to signal orders like marching or attacking. If the trumpet makes a confusing or muffled sound, the soldiers will not know what to do or how to get ready for battle. Unclear speech in church leaves people just as unprepared.

The same principle applies to Christians speaking in public worship. If the words spoken are not easy to understand, the listeners will learn nothing. The speaker might as well be wasting breath and talking into empty air.
There are hundreds of different languages spoken throughout the world. Every single one of them has clear meaning to the people who speak it. None of these languages is just meaningless noise.

If two people cannot understand each other's language, they appear as foreigners to one another. Neither one can grasp the other person's thoughts, and their words sound like mere babble. Speaking without being understood creates division instead of fellowship.

Since the Corinthians are excited about having spiritual gifts, Paul tells them how to use that enthusiasm well. They should seek and develop the gifts that help the whole church grow. True spiritual greatness is measured by how much good we do for others.

Anyone who speaks in an unknown tongue in the assembly should pray for the ability to translate what they say. That way, the meaning will not remain hidden from the congregation. Interpretation turns private worship into public blessing.

When someone prays in an unknown tongue, their own spirit is active in prayer, but their mind produces no fruit for the listeners. The words do not communicate thoughts that help anyone else learn. Public prayer must reach the minds of the hearers.

Paul decides that he will pray and sing with his spirit, but he will also pray and sing with his understanding. Christian worship needs both heartfelt devotion and clear thinking. Using our minds ensures that others can follow along and share in the praise.

If a leader gives thanks to God in an unknown tongue, an ordinary listener cannot say 'Amen' at the close of the prayer. Saying 'Amen' means agreeing with the prayer and making it one's own. No one can agree with words they do not understand.

The speaker may be offering a sincere and beautiful prayer of thanks to God. Even so, the person sitting nearby receives no spiritual help from it. Worship in church must always take into account the needs of the listeners.

Paul thanks God that he speaks in tongues more than all of the Corinthians. He mentions his own experience so they realize he is not speaking out of envy or ignorance. He values the gift, even while correcting its abuse.

In the public gathering of the church, Paul would rather speak five sensible words that instruct others than ten thousand words in a foreign language. The purpose of meeting together is to teach and help people, not to show off unusual talents.

Believers should stop acting like immature children who are fascinated only by noisy or showy things. Christians ought to be as innocent as newborn babies when it comes to malice and evil. In their thinking, however, they should be wise and mature adults.

Paul cites the Old Testament Scriptures, where God warned ancient Israel that He would speak to them through foreign armies with strange languages. Even after that discipline came, the rebellious people still refused to listen to God. Unintelligible language has often appeared alongside spiritual stubbornness.

Foreign tongues serve as a sign related to unbelievers rather than believers. Prophecy, by contrast, is given directly to instruct and strengthen those who already believe. The church should focus on the gift that builds up faith in its members.

differ.view: Methodists traditionally understand tongues as an outward miracle meant to prove God's power to unbelievers so they might accept the gospel.
Many evangelicals see tongues here as a sign of divine judgment against unbelief, like the foreign tongues that judged ancient Israel.

notes.meaning: If the whole church meets together and everyone starts speaking in unknown tongues at the same time, visiting unbelievers will be confused. They will assume the believers are out of their minds and acting like lunatics. Disorderly worship brings shame upon the Christian faith.

If everyone prophesies in clear, orderly speech, a visiting unbeliever will understand what is said. The truth reaches their conscience, and they feel convicted of their sins by the message. Clear teaching has the power to reach an outsider's heart.

The secret sins and thoughts of the visitor's heart are laid bare by God's word. The person is moved to fall facedown in reverence, worship God, and confess that God is truly present in the gathering. God's truth has a unique power to change lives when spoken plainly.

When believers gather for worship, different people bring a hymn, a teaching, a new insight, a tongue, or an interpretation. Paul gives one master rule to guide all these contributions: everything must be done to build up the church. Personal expression must always serve the good of the congregation.

If anyone speaks in a tongue during a meeting, only two or at most three should do so. They must speak one at a time, and someone must interpret what they say. Setting strict limits prevents confusion and keeps the meeting orderly.

If no one present has the gift of interpretation, the tongue-speaker must remain silent in the public meeting. That person may still use their gift quietly at home in private prayer with God. Public silence shows respect for the congregation's need to understand.

Only two or three prophets should speak at a single service. The other leaders and listeners must carefully weigh and evaluate what is spoken to ensure it matches God's true word. No human speaker is above testing by the Scriptures.

If someone sitting quietly receives a revelation from God, the person who is already speaking should yield the floor. Believers must be humble enough to give way to others rather than dominating the time. Courtesy and mutual respect keep church meetings peaceful.

All who have the gift of prophecy can take their turn to speak one by one. This orderly sharing allows the whole congregation to be taught and encouraged. God's truth works best when everyone has a chance to listen and learn.

Prophets remain in full control of their own spirits and speech. The Holy Spirit never drives believers into wild, uncontrollable actions or forces them to speak out of turn. True inspiration works alongside calm reason and self-control.

God is the Author of peace and good order, not of tumult and confusion. Christian worship should always display this peaceful harmony, just as it does in all the other assemblies of God's people. Disorder in church misrepresents the character of God.

Women are instructed to keep silent during the public worship assembly. They are not permitted to teach or lead the church, but are called to live in submission, as the Old Testament Scriptures teach. Order in worship respects God's created roles for men and women.

differ.view: Presbyterians and Reformed churches historically teach that this rule universally bars women from holding the public teaching office in church worship.
Methodists have held that this forbids women arguing or disrupting public worship, but does not stop them if God directly moves them to teach.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some modern scholars argue that verses 34 and 35 were not written by Paul here, pointing out that some ancient manuscripts place them after verse 40.

notes.meaning: If women want to learn more about something said in church, they should ask their own husbands at home. It was considered improper and disorderly for women to speak up and debate questions during public worship. Asking questions at home preserves peace in the congregation.

Paul rebukes the pride of the Corinthians by asking if God's word started with them or reached only them. They are not the mother church and have no right to invent their own disorderly practices while ignoring what other churches do. Believers must remain humble and willing to follow common standards.

Anyone who claims to be a prophet or truly spiritual must accept Paul's instructions as the Lord's own commands. A person who really has the Holy Spirit will gladly submit to apostolic authority. True spiritual maturity is proven by obedience to God's word.

If someone stubbornly refuses to accept these instructions, they should be left in their ignorance. The church should not waste its time arguing with those who will not be corrected. Rejecting apostolic instruction carries serious spiritual danger.

Paul concludes by encouraging believers to eagerly desire the gift of prophecy. At the same time, they must not forbid people from speaking in tongues when it is done properly. Every gift of the Spirit has its rightful place when guided by love.

Every part of Christian worship must be done with proper dignity, decency, and order. Meetings should never be noisy, confusing, or self-serving, but calm and reverent. God is honored when His people worship Him with peace and self-control.
